def test_even_odd_palindrome():
    # Known expected values
    assert even_odd_palindrome(1) == (0, 1)      # only 1 (odd palindrome)
    assert even_odd_palindrome(2) == (1, 1)      # 1 (odd), 2 (even)
    assert even_odd_palindrome(3) == (1, 2)      # 1, 3 odd; 2 even
    assert even_odd_palindrome(5) == (2, 3)      # 1,3,5 odd; 2,4 even
    assert even_odd_palindrome(9) == (4, 5)      # 1-9 all palindromes
    assert even_odd_palindrome(10) == (4, 5)     # 10 is not a palindrome
    assert even_odd_palindrome(11) == (4, 6)     # 11 is an odd palindrome
    assert even_odd_palindrome(12) == (4, 6)     # 12 is not a palindrome
    assert even_odd_palindrome(0) == (0, 0)      # empty range
    assert even_odd_palindrome(100) == (8, 10)   # even: 2,4,6,8,22,44,66,88; odd: 1,3,5,7,9,11,33,55,77,99

    # Cross-check against a brute-force reference for a range of inputs
    for n in range(0, 60):
        even = sum(1 for i in range(1, n + 1) if i % 2 == 0 and str(i) == str(i)[::-1])
        odd = sum(1 for i in range(1, n + 1) if i % 2 == 1 and str(i) == str(i)[::-1])
        assert even_odd_palindrome(n) == (even, odd), f"Failed for n={n}"

def test_even_odd_palindrome():
    # Basic small input
    assert even_odd_palindrome(1) == (0, 1)      # 1 is an odd palindrome
    assert even_odd_palindrome(2) == (1, 1)      # adds 2 (even palindrome)
    assert even_odd_palindrome(3) == (1, 2)      # adds 3 (odd palindrome)

    # Single digits 1-9: even palindromes {2,4,6,8}, odd {1,3,5,7,9}
    assert even_odd_palindrome(9) == (4, 5)

    # Two-digit palindromes 11..99 add 4 even (22,44,66,88) and 5 odd (11,33,55,77,99)
    assert even_odd_palindrome(10) == (4, 5)     # 10 is not a palindrome
    assert even_odd_palindrome(11) == (4, 6)     # 11 is an odd palindrome
    assert even_odd_palindrome(12) == (4, 6)     # 12 is not a palindrome
    assert even_odd_palindrome(22) == (5, 6)     # 22 is an even palindrome
    assert even_odd_palindrome(99) == (8, 10)    # all one/two-digit palindromes counted

    # Non-palindrome boundary values don't change counts
    assert even_odd_palindrome(100) == (8, 10)   # 100 is not a palindrome
    assert even_odd_palindrome(101) == (8, 11)   # 101 is an odd palindrome
    assert even_odd_palindrome(123) == (8, 13)   # adds 101, 111, 121 (all odd)

    # Edge cases
    assert even_odd_palindrome(0) == (0, 0)      # no numbers in range
    assert even_odd_palindrome(-5) == (0, 0)     # negative input -> empty range
